abstract: A 22-year-old man with primary mediastinal choriocarcinoma and bilateral lung metastases underwent an FDG PET/CT scan after completing chemotherapy. Serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin had normalized. PET/CT showed increased FDG uptake in the anterior mediastinal and lung lesions, suspicious for residual disease. After resection of the mediastinal and lung lesions, histopathology revealed necrosis and fibrohistiocytic reaction with no viable tumor. There was discordance between beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (negative) and FDG PET/CT (positive) findings, with PET/CT findings being false positive. Awareness of this potential pitfall of FDG PET/CT is important, and caution should be exercised when using FDG PET/CT to assess residual masses after chemotherapy.
abstract_ja: 22歳男性が原発性縦隔絨毛癌と両側肺転移を呈し、化学療法終了後にFDG PET/CT検査を受けた。血清β-hCGは正常化していた。PET/CTでは前縦隔および肺病変にFDG集積の増加を認め、残存病変が疑われた。縦隔および肺病変の切除後、病理組織学では壊死と線維組織球性反応がみられ、生存腫瘍は認められなかった。β-hCG(陰性)とFDG PET/CT(陽性)の所見は不一致であり、PET/CT所見は偽陽性であった。化学療法後の残存腫瘤評価にFDG PET/CTを用いる場合は、この落とし穴に注意し慎重に行うべきである。
